analysis.overall: A challenging 24 hours marked by stubborn highs overnight following a late meal, alongside mild lows caused by stacked correction insulin.

events.title: Late afternoon drop
events.description: Multiple small corrections aimed at a persistent high finally caught up around 4:30 PM, pulling glucose down to 64 mg/dL.

events.title: Late dinner spike
events.description: Bolusing 4.1u for a 45g late dinner, followed shortly by a extra carb correction, sparked a steep upward trend into the night.

events.title: Overnight peak
events.description: Glucose hit 249 mg/dL during the night and resisted initial corrections, keeping readings elevated until well after 4:00 AM.

events.title: Morning low
events.description: The tail end of overnight correction insulin drove readings down to a low of 62 mg/dL before breakfast.

events.title: Breakfast handling
events.description: Bolusing 6.1u for 65g of carbs helped keep the breakfast rise controlled, peaking gently under 180 mg/dL.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Be cautious with stacking multiple small correction boluses close together, as active insulin built up and caused sharp drops in both the afternoon and early morning.
